rows.row_quote: quartz interlayered with fine to medium grained, strongly hematized quartz rich layers, containing locally chloritized mafics and kaolinized felsics - the effects of faulting are seen as locally occurring and to varying degrees of intensity, fracturing, shearing and brecciation, the core is strongly broken up locally, but otherwise gives the impression of having been rehealed - any apparent foliation (gneissosity?) may owe its origin more to tectonics (shear flowage) than to a remmant of pre-existing gneissosity - probably represents a anatectic pegmatite conponent of a granitic gneiss * @ 165.0-182.3 m, the second unit which possesses a mottled maroon, dark green and grey appearance consists of strongly hematized and chloritized essentially equigranular medium grained cataclastic rock of probable granitic gneiss origin, other identifiable mineral is quartz occurring as individual grains and thin crosscutting quartz veinlets - within this interval areaswere locally sheared to the point of having angular quartz fragments "floating" in a maroon hematitic fault gouge i.e. @ 172.1-172.9m (shear breccia) - the occurrence and intensity of faulting is also variable within this interval - a weak "foliation" is locally apparent which may once again owe its origin to faulting, elsewhere it appears massive - 130 c/s @ 166.0 m, background of 25-50 c/s - 95 c/s @ 165.3 m similiar background to above
